title: 1972 AHSME Problem 2
statement: If a dealer could get his goods for \(8\%\) less while keeping his selling price fixed, his profit, based on cost, would be increased to \((x+10)\%\) from his present profit of \(x\%,\) which is:

solutions.text:
The fixed selling price gives \[ \begin{aligned} 1+0.01x&=0.92\\ &\quad+0.0092(x+10). \end{aligned} \] Simplifying yields \[ 1+0.01x=1.012+0.0092x, \] so \(0.0008x=0.012\) and \(x=15.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let the present cost be \(C\) and express the same selling price in two ways
The reduced cost is \(0.92C\) and its profit rate is \((x+10)\%\)
